patch.value: Give assurance a declared noun placement and history-author-acknowledge a history leaf: the two live commands whose consolidation owners closed without moving them

## Scope
Two live top-level commands lost their consolidation owner when the owning items closed without moving them.

1. assurance is an SDK-owned governance surface (measurements, assertions, gates) with no noun in the twelve-noun grammar. Decide its placement with a recorded pbyu ruling: an ops assurance leaf (diagnostics family, where the census currently points), or a keep-as-is exception because it is a first-class data noun like plan. Whichever is chosen, the destination row flips from consolidation to target_noun or keep_as_is.
2. history-author-acknowledge is the only history-* spelling still registered at the root. Give it a canonical leaf under the history noun (history acknowledge, matching the shared verb vocabulary) with the root spelling kept as a hidden permanent alias, and carry the relocation through contracts, completions, MCP action parity and docs.

## Constraints
Zero feature loss; the help-token budget for the affected commands has zero headroom, so the new leaf's help must not exceed the text it replaces. Positional shape count stays within its budget.

A pbyu ruling records where assurance lives in the noun grammar and the destination row flips from consolidation to target_noun or keep_as_is; pm history acknowledge (or the shared-verb spelling the ruling picks) is the canonical leaf; history-author-acknowledge remains executable as a hidden permanent alias with identical arguments, results and exit codes; Contracts, shell completions, MCP action parity and docs reflect the relocation and the command-grammar gate passes with no positional-shape or help-token budget growth
assurance has a recorded noun disposition and history-author-acknowledge resolves to a canonical history leaf with its root spelling as a hidden permanent alias.
